findings.title: enableSqlExpressions always returns false regardless of feature flag state
findings.body: The function `enableSqlExpressions` computes `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` and then unconditionally returns `false` in both branches. This means SQL expressions are permanently disabled even when the `sqlExpressions` feature flag is explicitly enabled by an administrator. The intent (per the PR description and the CVE-2024-9264 fix) is to disable SQL expressions by default for security, but the implementation makes the feature flag non-functional: there is no configuration under which SQL expressions can be turned on. If the goal is a hard kill-switch, the feature-flag check should be removed entirely and the function deleted; if the goal is a default-off flag, the function should return the value of `h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` (or its negation, depending on flag semantics). As written, the dead conditional is misleading and the flag documented in the linked docs has no effect.

This message is factually wrong: SQL expressions are implemented (see `pkg/expr/sql_command.go` and `pkg/expr/sql/`), they are deliberately disabled as a security measure for CVE-2024-9264. Returning "not implemented" to API consumers will cause confusion and may lead users to believe the feature is simply unavailable rather than intentionally disabled for security. The error should state that SQL expressions are disabled (e.g., "sqlExpressions are disabled" or reference the feature flag), so users and support staff understand the actual reason and know how to look for the relevant configuration.

findings.title: Stub DB methods return "not implemented" errors that are reachable and mishandled

These stubs are still wired into live code paths: `pkg/expr/sql/parser.go:TablesList` calls `duckDB.RunCommands(...)` (line 26) and `pkg/expr/sql_command.go:NewSQLCommand` calls `sql.TablesList(rawSQL)` (line 30), and `SQLCommand.Execute` calls `db.QueryFramesInto(...)` (line 100). Although `pkg/expr/reader.go` currently blocks the `QueryTypeSQL` path, the older/unmarshal path via `UnmarshalSQLCommand` (pkg/expr/sql_command.go:51) still constructs `SQLCommand` through `NewSQLCommand`, which will now always fail with a generic "error reading SQL command" wrapping the "not implemented" error from the stub. If any code path reaches `SQLCommand.Execute` (e.g., the legacy expression pipeline that does not go through `ExpressionQueryReader.ReadQuery`), it will hit `db.QueryFramesInto` and return the "not implemented" error to the user as a query failure. The stub should either be removed along with the dead SQL command code, or the SQL command construction/execution paths should be fully removed rather than left as landmines that produce confusing errors.

findings.title: Dead code: rsp.Values is overwritten when frame has zero rows
findings.body: In `SQLCommand.Execute`, when `frame.Rows() == 0` the code sets `rsp.Values` to a `mathexp.NoData` value (lines 110-114), but then unconditionally overwrites `rsp.Values` with `mathexp.TableData{Frame: frame}` at lines 116-118. The `NoData` branch is therefore dead code and has no effect. This is a pre-existing bug (not introduced by this diff), but it is in a file touched by this security fix and affects the behavior of the SQL expression path: empty results are returned as an empty table rather than as NoData, which may affect how the frontend renders empty SQL expression results. The `if frame.Rows() == 0` block should either be removed or the unconditional assignment should be made conditional (e.g., `else`).

findings.title: SQL string is interpolated into a DuckDB command without parameterization, relying on a naive quote-escaping heuristic
findings.body: `TablesList` builds a DuckDB command via `fmt.Sprintf("SELECT json_serialize_sql('%s')", rawSQL)` after only replacing single quotes with doubled single quotes (`strings.Replace(rawSQL, "'", "''", -1)`). This is a hand-rolled escaping scheme that is applied to user-supplied SQL before it is sent to the database engine. While the SQL expression path is currently disabled by the reader, this function remains reachable via `NewSQLCommand`/`UnmarshalSQLCommand` (see pkg/expr/sql_command.go:30), which does not check the feature flag. The escaping only handles single quotes and does not account for other SQL injection vectors (e.g., backslash escapes depending on DuckDB string literal semantics, or the fact that the input is itself SQL being embedded inside another SQL statement). This is exactly the class of vulnerability that CVE-2024-9264 addressed. Since the DuckDB dependency is being removed and the stub returns "not implemented", the cleanest fix is to delete this function and the entire SQL expression execution path rather than leave an unsafe string-interpolation helper in the codebase. If the code is kept, the raw SQL must never be embedded into another SQL statement via string formatting.

findings.title: Malformed comment on indirect dependency line
findings.body: Line 463 reads `github.com/fxamacker/cbor/v2 v2.7.0 // indirect; indirect0.0.0-20240809095826-8eb5495c0b2a`. The comment contains a corrupted version string (`indirect0.0.0-20240809095826-8eb5495c0b2a`) that appears to be a merge/rebase artifact where a version string was accidentally concatenated with the `// indirect` marker. This is a malformed `go.mod` comment. While Go tooling ignores trailing comments on require lines, this is clearly unintended text that should be cleaned up to just `// indirect` (the version is already specified in the require directive itself).
